findings.claim: After taking the write lock, the code does not check the cache again. On a cold or nil cache, every request that saw ret == nil waits for the lock in turn and then re-reads and re-parses assets-manifest.json (or re-fetches from the CDN once that path is enabled). This repeats the work without fixing anything.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from webassets.go:41-49 and 69-70; nothing was run. The result is still correct and race-free; the cost is wasted cold-start work. Proposed fix from all four seats: after Lock(), add `if cfg.Env != setting.Dev && entryPointAssetsCache != nil { return entryPointAssetsCache, nil }`.
findings.reason: Raised by all four seats. The fix is a small double-check that keeps the existing pattern. This is a Minor finding, so the red-test rule does not apply, but a concurrent cold-cache test counting manifest reads could guard it.

findings.claim: In setting.Dev, every call skips the cache and holds the exclusive lock while reading the manifest file. Index, frontend-settings and recovery-page requests in dev are therefore served one at a time on file I/O, where before they ran in parallel (racily).
findings.evidence: Reasoned from webassets.go:45-70. Dev only, with no production impact. The output is correct; the cost is latency.
findings.reason: Dev-only latency with no correctness impact, and the re-check fix does not change it because dev always reloads. Defer with a `ponytail:` comment noting the dev serialization.

findings.claim: The data-race fix ships without a regression test. No test calls GetWebAssets from several goroutines, so nothing guards the fix.
findings.evidence: contribute/create-pull-request.md:28: "the pull request should include tests that replicate the fixed bug". The existing TestReadWebassets and TestReadWebassetsFromCDN are single-goroutine and the test file is unchanged. Proposed test: N goroutines calling GetWebAssets against a temp StaticRootPath/build/assets-manifest.json copied from testdata/sample-assets-manifest.json, run under `go test -race ./pkg/api/webassets/`. It should report a race on base cca9dee702 and pass on head b1613e320a. Not run.
findings.reason: Three seats agree, and the repo's PR guidelines require a test for bug fixes. Severity normalised to Important because a documented standard requires it. The proposed race test is the red test: it should fail on the base and stay in the suite as the guard.

findings.claim: The patch keeps the package-level cache and adds a second global (the mutex), which goes against the documented standard to avoid global state. The added `// TODO: get rid of global state` admits the problem without fixing it.
findings.evidence: contribute/backend/style-guide.md:185-189, contribute/backend/recommended-practices.md:46-54, contribute/backend/services.md:5. Both seats note the global existed before the patch and that moving to DI is out of scope.
findings.reason: Raised by two seats, so it goes in the appendix and is not fixed. The global predates the patch.

findings.claim: The RWMutex is heavier than the work it does. An atomic.Pointer[dtos.EntryPointAssets] with Load/Store would behave the same, drop the mutex variable and all the Lock/Unlock lines, and be about 3 lines shorter.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from lines 35-49 and 69-70. Go 1.22 per go.mod. No file in pkg/ uses atomic.Pointer yet. superpowers considered this and set it aside as style.
findings.reason: Raised by one seat and advisory only, so it goes in the appendix and is not fixed.

findings.claim: In production, a missing or broken manifest leaves the cache nil after each failed load. Every later request then retries the failed read under the exclusive lock, one at a time.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. The error path stores a nil result at line 69. open-code-review saw this behaviour but did not report it, because it is unchanged from before the patch.
findings.reason: Raised by one seat, so it goes in the appendix. The nil-on-error behaviour predates the patch.

findings.claim: If the CDN branch is enabled, the exclusive lock would be held across the HTTP call in readWebAssetsFromCDN, blocking every other caller during the fetch.
findings.evidence: Reasoned. The path is currently dead (`cdn := ""` at line 54). open-code-review noted the same and judged it not a real risk until the branch is enabled.
findings.reason: Raised by one seat and only reachable through dead code, so it goes in the appendix.

findings.claim: The package-level cache leaks between tests in the package because nothing resets it.
findings.evidence: Reasoned from the global entryPointAssetsCache. No reset hook exists.
findings.reason: Raised by one seat, so it goes in the appendix. The behaviour predates the patch.

findings.claim: The commit subject "fix data race in GetWebAssets" lacks the required Area prefix.
findings.evidence: contribute/create-pull-request.md:94 and :125 (`<Area>: <Summary>`). The seat notes that Grafana squashes on merge and uses the PR title as the subject.
findings.reason: Raised by one advisory seat, so it goes in the appendix. It only matters if this commit subject becomes the PR title.

coverage: Files skipped: none. The patch touches one file, pkg/api/webassets/webassets.go, and all four seats reviewed it in full, along with its callers pkg/api/index.go:82, pkg/api/frontendsettings.go:62 and pkg/middleware/recovery.go:141. Gate: not run (benchmark mode), so the review is unanchored and no finding has executed ground truth. Standards axis did run (CONTRIBUTING.md, contribute/create-pull-request.md, contribute/backend/style-guide.md, recommended-practices.md, services.md).
